senses.gloss: लुप् (I) vi. 4P (pres. लुप्यति) 1. To be confused or disordered; 2. to vanish.

लुप् (II) vt. 6U (pp. लुप्त; pres. लुंपति-ते; freq. लोलुप्यते) 1. To break, to cut off, to mutilate; 2. to rob, to plunder, to deprive of; 3. to seize, to pounce upon; 4. to suppress, to cause to disappear.With वि-, 1. to cut off, to break off; 2. to carry away, to seize, to rob, to plunder; 3. to destroy, to ruin, क्रव्याद्भिरंगलतिका नियतं विलुप्ता Ut.iii, R.xv.2; 4. to efface, to wipe off, Na.xxii.54.
लुप्त (I) a. (f. प्ता) 1. Broken, cut off, injured, destroyed; 2. robbed, deprived of; 3. lost, disappeared; 4. omitted, neglected, (pp. of लुप् q.v.).
लुप्त (I) a. (f. प्ता) 1. Broken, cut off, injured, destroyed; 2. robbed, deprived of; 3. lost, disappeared; 4. omitted, neglected, (pp. of लुप् q.v.).
लुप्त-उपमा f. an elliptical simile (i.e. one in which one or more of the four requisites are not expressed). See पूर्णोपमा.
लुप्त-प्रतिज्ञ a. false to one’s promise.
